# Report: region_003

**Sequence:** 3,000 bp; overall GC content 49.1%; A/G-rich tail at the 5' end (GC 38–42% in nt 1–300) rising to 53–57% across most of the rest of the sequence.

## Notable feature — one strong open reading frame

The sequence contains a single, very conspicuous coding region and is otherwise largely unremarkable. Details:

**Coordinates (1-based):** NT 1327 – 2535, on the **+ strand**, reading frame 1.
- The upstream in-frame stop codon is at **1324–1326 (TAA)**. The very next position, **1327**, begins a **1,209-nt stretch containing no stop codon at all**, terminating at a TGA stop codon at **2536–2538**.
- The first in-frame ATG (start codon) occurs at **1341–1343**, giving a protein of **~398 aa** from this ATG (the full stop-to-stop read-through is 1,209 nt ≈ 402 aa + stop).

**Why this is the standout feature (frame-0 stop codon statistics):**

| | + strand, frame 0 | all other frames |
|---|---|---|
| Number of stop codons | **20** | 11–51 in each of the other five frames |
| Largest stop-to-stop gap | **1,209 nt** (1327–2535) | 693 nt is the next longest anywhere (+ strand frame 0, 106–795); the longest on the − strand is only 339 nt |

A 1,209-nt gap without a stop codon is highly unlikely by chance in a sequence whose background GC is near 50%, where a stop codon would be expected roughly every ~90–100 bp in a random read. Frames 1 and 2 (and the whole minus strand) show a normal, random-looking distribution of stops, so this is a genuine long ORF, not a GC-content artifact.

**Supporting evidence that the ORF is real coding sequence, not just a stop-free stretch:**
- It has a distinct **codon-bias signature** relative to the flanking sequence: GC at first and third codon positions is elevated (GC1 55.6%, GC3 55.6%) while GC2 is at 43.4%, producing the tell-tale "GC3 skew" of real coding regions.
- The downstream flanking sequence also looks like a gene's 3' neighbourhood: a run of **A/T-rich tracts at nt 2536–2600** and the region is followed by elevated GC in the 2700–2999 block — consistent with transcriptional polarity rather than an isolated artifact.
- The predicted protein is a plausible ~45 kDa globular-type protein with a normal, non-biased amino-acid composition (rich in A, R, K, Q, L, S — no extreme hydrophobicity, no stretches of a single residue, no signals of low complexity).
- Near the 5' end of the ORF there is a plausible ** Shine–Dalgarno-like motif: "AGGA" is present at nt 21** relative to the upstream stop (near 1290–1293), which sits only a short distance upstream of the ORF start at 1341 — although the intervening spacing (~45 nt) is larger than the canonical 5–10 nt RBS-to-start distance, so this is weak, circumstantial support only.

## Everything else — nothing notable
- The rest of the 3,000 bp (nt 1–1326 and 2539–3000) contains only short gaps between stop codons (typically 100–250 nt) in all six frames, all consistent with random, non-coding sequence.
- A few short homopolymers exist (TTTTTT at nt 55–60 and 228–232; AAAAAA at 2982–2987) but these are unremarkable in a 3 kb piece.
- No strong hairpin/cis-element: the longest perfect inverted repeat is only a 9-bp stem (fwd arm at 1533–1541, rev arm at 1559–1567), which is not unusual for non-repetitive DNA.
- No long tandem or direct repeats, no transposon-like features that I could detect directly.

## Bottom line
There is one striking feature: a single, well-defined open reading frame at **NT 1327–2535 (+ strand, frame 1)**, ~402 codons long (predicted ~398 aa from the ATG at NT 1341), with a stop codon at NT 2536–2538. Its codon-composition and stop-free length make it almost certainly a real protein-coding gene with an intact start codon and no frameshifts. I cannot identify its function or homologs from sequence alone without a database, but it is very likely a bona fide ~45 kDa protein-coding gene; the rest of region_003 carries no other notable features.
